text.p: Bonds outperformed Spain at the long end and the lack of paper is likely to keep the spread between the two 10-year cash markets at more than 10 basis points, traders said.
"The spread in the 10 years is too negative compared with Spain but as long as there is not more paper on offer, either from the Treasury of the market, it will not narrow," said one trader.
"Monday we will follow Spain but the 10 years are going to continue stronger than bonos," added another.
The negative spread in the 10 years contrasted with the short end where Spain was at a premium and the middle part of the yield curve where the spread was flat.

But some traders said that Portuguese yields should not really be above those of Spain because while there is a differential between the two countries' central bank rates, it was certain that the Bank of Portugal would be making fresh rate cuts.
